output.root_problem: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to 1180-1260/month in Aug-Sep 2026 (E-05), and 59% of the disputed bills were billed from ACTUAL meter reads, not ESTIMATED ones (E-01). With a tariff/rate change (E-02) and a customer-service response-time shortfall (E-03) both ruled out, the dominant mechanism is a defect in the billing import/validation step that is producing incorrect bills from otherwise-valid actual meter reads, rather than field-read delays driving estimate substitution.
output.requested_solution: SH-CS requested an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing wrong bills.
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume doubled from ~600/month to 1180-1260/month starting August 2026 (E-05).
59% of disputed bills were billed from ACTUAL meter reads versus 41% ESTIMATED (E-01).
Field manual-read route completion fell to 88% vs a 95% target across 9200 accounts in Aug-Sep (E-04).
Customer service response times remain within SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d vs 3.0d) despite the ticket volume surge (E-03).
causal_chain: Reads are collected via AMI or field manual read and pass MDMS validation (P-M2C steps 1-2).

The billing import + validation step processes these reads into bills; something in this step (candidate: a billing validation rule change, H-RULE-CHANGE-DEFECT) began mishandling a subset of actual-read bills around August, rather than those reads going through estimate substitution.
59% of all disputed bills carry ACTUAL (not estimated) read type (E-01), evidencing this actual-read billing path as the dominant disputed segment.
A tariff/rate change (E-02) and a ticket-response capacity gap (E-03) have been ruled out as alternative explanations for the surge.
Customers dispute the resulting incorrect bills, driving CRM dispute ticket volume from ~600/month to 1180-1260/month in Aug-Sep (E-05).

assumptions.statement: It is assumed the dominant disputed-bill mechanism is a billing import/validation defect rather than some other unidentified actual-read billing issue, since no billing-config evidence has yet confirmed this.
The read-type split in E-01 (59% actual / 41% estimated) is assumed representative of the full Aug-Sep surge, not a sampling or query artifact.
CRM dispute_volume_monthly counts (E-05) are assumed to reflect distinct billing complaints, not duplicate tickets per bill or per customer.
SH-FIELD's staffing-shortage narrative (E-07) is assumed only partially explanatory since it is a non-authoritative claim not yet joined to the disputed-bill dataset.
